Success criteria: The card box must be inside the basket, close to and touching its body, and completely clear of the table. Both basket and box must be clearly raised above their starting positions, with the opening upright and without excessive tilt. Sliding the basket across the table is insufficient.

## Execution tips

- Grasp the middle of opposing straight card-box sidewalls, opening slightly wider than its width in that direction. Confirm fingers surround the walls without pressing the table before closing to avoid pushing the thin box away.
- Arched handles occupy space near the basket opening. Choose a passage based on the combined box-and-gripper width, and complete needed rotation above the rim to avoid catching a handle or leaving the box bridging the rim during descent.
- Lower the card box close to the basket bottom and release only after confirming the bottom supports it, reducing bouncing or tipping from a drop.
- When grasping the basket, choose a straight rim section away from the card box and handle joints. Grip with one finger inside and one outside, fully contacting both walls with the pads to avoid slipping from pinching only the very top.
- When carrying a loaded basket, keep its opening facing up and lift and turn smoothly, reducing the chance of the card box sliding toward the edge or falling out.
